questions.text:
Consider socket API on a Linux machine that supports connected UDP sockets. A connected UDP socket is a UDP socket on which connect function has already been called. Which of the following statements is/are CORRECT ?
I. A connected UDP socket can be used to communicate with multiple peers simultaneously.
II. A process can successfully call connect function again for an already connected UDP socket.
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- I: a connected UDP socket is tied to one peer; datagrams from others are ignored False
- II: calling connect again on a UDP socket is allowed (to change the peer or disconnect) True

Answer: II only

questions.text:
Consider the following statements about the routing protocols, Routing Information Protocol (RIP) and Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) in an IPv4 network.

I. RIP uses distance vector routing
II. RIP packets are sent using UDP
III. OSPF packets are sent using TCP
IV. OSPF operation is based on link-state routing

Which of the statements above are CORRECT?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- RIP is distance-vector True and runs over UDP (port 520) True
- OSPF is link-state True, but runs directly over IP (protocol 89), not TCP False

Answer: I, II and IV only

questions.text:
The values of parameters for the Stop-and-Wait ARQ protocol are as given below:

Bit rate of the transmission channel = 1Mbps
Propagation delay from sender to receiver = 0.75 ms
Time to process a frame = 0.25ms
Number of bytes in the information frame =1980
Number of bytes in the acknowledge frame = 20
Number of overhead bytes in the information frame = 20

Assume that there are no transmission errors. Then the transmission efficiency ( expressed in percentage) of the Stop-and - Wait ARQ protocol for the above parameters is _________( correct to 2 decimal places)
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Frame transmission: 1980 [latex]\times[/latex] 8 / [latex]10^6[/latex] = 15.84 ms (useful data 1960 bytes = 15.68 ms)
- ACK transmission: 20 [latex]\times[/latex] 8 / [latex]10^6[/latex] = 0.16 ms
- Propagation: 0.75 ms each way; processing 0.25 ms

Cycle = 15.84 + 0.75 + 0.25 + 0.16 + 0.75 = 17.75 ms
Efficiency = 15.68 / 17.75 [latex]\approx[/latex] 88.34%

Answer: 88.34

questions.text:
In a RSA cryptosystem a participant A uses two prime numbers p=13 and q=17 to generate
her public and private keys. If the public key of A is 35. Then the private key of A is
__________.
questions.solution:
n = 13 [latex]\times[/latex] 17 = 221, [latex]\phi(n)=12\times16=192[/latex]. Private key d satisfies [latex]35d\equiv1\pmod{192}[/latex].

[latex]35\times11=385=2\times192+1[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] d = 11

Answer: 11

questions.text:
A computer network uses polynomials over GF(2) for error checking with 8 bits as
information bits and uses [latex]x^{3}+x+1[/latex] as the generator polynomial to generate the check bits. In
this network, the message 01011011 is transmitted as
questions.solution:
Generator [latex]x^3+x+1[/latex] = 1011. Append 3 zeros to 01011011 and divide: 01011011000 [latex]\div[/latex] 1011 leaves remainder 101.

Transmitted = 01011011 101

Answer: 01011011101
